Admin.PerUserHow:
This copy of Mesura runs from {0}, a folder that any program you run can change. Mesura never asks for administrator rights from such a folder: a program that replaced Mesura.exe there would be started with full rights the next time you approved the prompt. So changes to the whole PC are skipped here, and everything that doesn't need administrator rights works as usual.

To get full access, install Mesura for all users (Program Files): run the installer from an administrator prompt with ALLUSERS=1, for example msiexec /i Mesura-<version>-x64.msi ALLUSERS=1 (installing.md in the documentation has the details). Technical reason: {1}.

Settings.RestorePoint: Make a restore point before changing the whole PC
Settings.RestorePointHint: A System Restore point before changes for the whole PC, when Mesura runs as administrator. Windows makes one per 24 hours; Undo in Activity covers the rest.
Firmware.Title: BIOS & Firmware
Firmware.StatusNone: Nothing worth changing in the firmware.
Firmware.FailedHint: Nothing was changed. Try Recheck; the session log on Activity has the reason.
Firmware.RestartAsk: Windows will restart in ten seconds into the BIOS/UEFI setup. Save your work first.
Firmware.RestartNote: Mesura changes nothing in the BIOS itself: you choose each setting there, and save or leave without saving. After the restart, open this page to see what changed.
Firmware.RestartNotUefi: This PC started in legacy BIOS mode, so Windows can't restart it into the setup. Restart, and press the BIOS key (usually Delete or F2) right after the logo appears.
Firmware.RestartViaSettings: Asking the firmware to open its setup needs administrator rights, which Mesura doesn't have in this window. Windows Settings can do it from a normal account: Recovery > Advanced startup > Restart now, then Troubleshoot > Advanced options > UEFI Firmware Settings.
Firmware.RestartScheduledHint: It will open the BIOS setup. Cancel here, or run shutdown /a, to stay.
Firmware.RestartFailed: Windows didn't restart into the setup
Firmware.RestartFailedHint: Nothing was changed. Use Settings > Recovery > Advanced startup instead.
Firmware.Obs.memory.soldered: The memory is soldered to the board: there is no profile or slot choice to make.
Firmware.Obs.memory.at-rating: Memory runs at {0} MT/s, the {1} MT/s its part number says it is sold at.
Firmware.Obs.memory.below-rating: Memory runs at {0} MT/s, but its part number ({2}) says it is sold at {1} MT/s: the profile is probably off.
Firmware.Obs.memory.above-base: Memory runs at {0} MT/s, above the base speed of {1}: a profile is on.
Firmware.Obs.memory.base-speed: Memory runs at {0} MT/s, the base speed of {1}. Windows can't read what the kit is rated for (part number: {2}); if it's a gaming kit, its profile is off.
Firmware.Obs.memory.single: One memory module in a board with {1} slots: single channel, half the bandwidth.
Firmware.Obs.memory.same-channel: Both modules report the same channel ({0}): probably single channel.
Firmware.Obs.memory.dual: The modules sit in different channels: dual channel.
Firmware.Obs.memory.crowded: {0} modules: all channels used. Four modules often limit the speed the board can hold stable.
Firmware.Obs.rebar.no-card: No graphics card with its own memory in this PC.
Firmware.Obs.rebar.needs-uefi: {0}: Resizable BAR needs UEFI boot, and this PC starts in legacy mode.
Firmware.Obs.rebar.unreadable: {0} ({1} MB of memory): Windows didn't report its memory window.
Firmware.Obs.rebar.on: {0}: the memory window is {1} MB for {2} MB of memory: Resizable BAR is on.
Firmware.Obs.rebar.off: {0}: the memory window is {1} MB for {2} MB of memory: Resizable BAR is off.
Firmware.Obs.bios.intel-microcode-old: {1} is in Intel's guidance on 13th and 14th generation instability; the microcode here is {0}, older than 0x12B, the final fix.
Firmware.Obs.bios.intel-microcode-ok: Microcode {0}: at or past Intel's final fix (0x12B) for 13th and 14th generation instability.
Firmware.Obs.bios.intel-microcode-unknow: {0} is in Intel's guidance on 13th and 14th generation instability, and Windows didn't report its microcode, so it can't be checked from here.
Firmware.Obs.bios.age: This BIOS is about {0} months old. A newer one may exist; Mesura can't see.
Firmware.Obs.boot.legacy: Windows starts in legacy BIOS mode: Resizable BAR, Secure Boot and Windows 11 need UEFI.
Firmware.Obs.sb.legacy: Secure Boot can't be on: this PC starts in legacy mode.
Firmware.Obs.tpm.on: A TPM {0} is present and working.
Firmware.Obs.virt.hypervisor: Windows is running on a hypervisor, so virtualization is on.
Firmware.Obs.virt.on: Virtualization is on in the firmware.
Firmware.Obs.virt.off: Virtualization is off in the firmware. Only virtual machines, WSL 2 and Android emulators need it.
Firmware.Obs.boost.portable: A laptop's boost and power limits are the maker's choice and are rarely exposed.
Firmware.Obs.boost.amd: {0}: Windows can't read Precision Boost Overdrive or Curve Optimizer, so Mesura can't say what is set.
Firmware.Obs.boost.intel: {0}: Windows can't read the board's power limits or boost options, so Mesura can't say what is set.
Firmware.Obs.pcie.check: {0}: Windows reports what the card can do, not always what it is doing, so there is no verdict; a render test shows the real link.
Start.Title: Administrator rights
Start.Message: Some changes (power plans, Windows policies, services, restore points) need administrator rights; the rest works without them. Which do you want for this session?
Start.Remember: Remember my choice (change it in Settings)
Start.SharedMessage: This copy runs from a folder any program you run can change, so Mesura never restarts itself with administrator rights here: changes to the whole PC are skipped, and everything else works.
Restore.Failure.ProtectionOff: System Protection is off, so Windows can't make one. Turn it on in System Properties > System Protection.
Restore.Failure.Unavailable: System Restore isn't available on this Windows: its component is missing or fails to load.
Restore.Failure.AccessDenied: Windows refused: it needs administrator rights.
Restore.Failure.Skipped: Windows makes one automatic point per 24 hours and skipped this one. Undo in Activity still covers this run.
Restore.Failure.Other: Windows couldn't make one. The details are under Technical details.
System.Title: System
System.Footer: Read from Windows and the firmware; nothing is changed. Serial numbers, network addresses, product keys and user names are neither read nor included in the report.
System.FailedHint: Nothing was changed. Try Refresh; the session log on Activity has the reason.
System.CopyFailed: Couldn't copy the report: another program is using the clipboard
System.SaveFailedHint: Choose another folder, one you can write to.
Settings.CheckUpdates: Check for updates when Mesura starts
Settings.CheckUpdatesHint: Nothing is downloaded or installed until you choose.
Settings.ChannelHint: Stable gets finished releases. Preview gets release candidates earlier, with rougher edges.
Update.Headline: Mesura {0} is available
Update.DoneText: Your settings, history and profiles are as you left them.
Update.FailedText: Mesura {0} is still the version installed. {1}
Update.ReasonUntrusted: The downloaded files didn't pass the check that they are the official ones, so nothing was installed.
Update.ReasonStillOpen: Mesura didn't close in time, so nothing was changed.
Update.ReasonBusy: Windows was busy with another installation. Try again in a minute.
Update.ReasonAdmin: Installing needs administrator rights, and they weren't given.
Update.ReasonRolledBack: The installer stopped part-way and put the previous version back.
Update.ReasonFiles: The downloaded files couldn't be read.
Update.ReasonOther: The installer reported an error; the details are in the update log in Mesura's data folder.
Update.Skipped: Version {0} will not be offered again.
Update.Offline: Couldn't reach the update server: no internet connection.
Update.Timeout: The update server didn't answer in time.
Update.ServerError: The update server had a problem.
Update.NotPublished: No update has been published yet.
Update.Refused: The update information didn't pass verification and was ignored.
Update.FailureHint: Mesura keeps working as it is. Try again later.
Update.DownloadHint: Nothing was installed. You can try again.
Update.DownloadOffline: The download was interrupted: no internet connection.
Update.DiskFull: Not enough free disk space to download the update.
Update.AccessDenied: Mesura couldn't save the update in its data folder.
Update.Corrupt: The downloaded file is damaged or isn't the official one, so it was deleted.
Update.DownloadServer: The server couldn't provide the update file.
Update.PortableMessage: This copy of Mesura wasn't set up by the installer, so it can't replace itself. The verified installer opens next; it installs Mesura properly (you choose the folder) and keeps your settings, history and profiles.
Update.RestartMessage: Mesura closes, installs version {0} and opens again. Your settings, history and profiles stay. If the installation fails, the previous version is put back.
Update.ElevationDeclined: Installing for all users needs administrator rights, and they weren't given. Nothing was changed.
Update.UpdaterNotStarted: The updater didn't start. Nothing was changed.
Update.Safe: The update is downloaded from the official release and checked against a signature only the Mesura author can make before anything is installed.
Update.DoneRestart: Windows was still using some of Mesura's files, so they are replaced when Windows restarts. Restart Windows to finish the update.
Apps.ChoiceCountMesura: Mesura's prepared settings for {0} of {1} chosen apps; the others install as they are.
Apps.ChoiceCountCustom: Your saved settings for {0} of {1} chosen apps; the others install as they are.
Apps.ChoiceMesuraNone: Mesura has no prepared settings for these apps; they install as they are.
Apps.ChoiceCustomNone: Your saved settings don't cover these apps; they install as they are.
Apps.ConfigBlockedShort: Mesura runs as another account than the signed-in user, so it doesn't set up app settings.
